title: Algorithmic Problem Solving: Longest Common Prefix String Scanning
concepts_and_definitions: Longest Common Prefix (LCP) – the longest string that is a prefix of all strings in a set
Binary Search – divide‑and‑conquer technique to locate a target value within a sorted range
Hash Set – data structure for O(1) average‑time membership checks, used to count character occurrences
Time Complexity – Big‑O notation describing algorithm efficiency, e.g., O(n·m) for LCP and O(n·log M) for banana‑eating
Greedy Strategy – choosing the locally optimal speed in the banana‑eating problem to minimize hours
mechanisms_and_formulas: Binary Search Update Rules: if prefix is common, low = mid+1; else high = mid-1
Banana‑Eating Time Formula: hours = Σ ceil(pile_i / speed)
LCP Character Comparison Loop: for each position j, compare s[0][j] with s[i][j] for all i
factual_summary_text:
The session revisited two classic algorithmic challenges: finding the longest common prefix (LCP) among a list of strings and determining the minimum eating speed for a banana‑eating problem. For the LCP, the instructor emphasized a straightforward character‑by‑character comparison across all strings, breaking out of the loop when a mismatch occurs and returning the accumulated prefix. The discussion highlighted the importance of early termination and the use of a hash set to count character occurrences when checking for common prefixes.

The banana‑eating problem was approached with a binary search over possible speeds. The lecturer explained how to compute the total hours required for a given speed using the formula ∑ ceil(pile_i / speed) and how to adjust the search bounds based on whether the computed time exceeds the allowed hours. Throughout the lecture, code snippets were examined, memory allocation in Java was clarified (reference vs. garbage collection), and students were prompted to identify potential improvements in the provided implementations.

Overall, the class combined theoretical explanations of binary search and greedy strategies with practical code reviews, reinforcing concepts such as time complexity analysis, loop invariants, and efficient data structure usage.
